newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian papers wary of new Pakistan administration.
newsitem.headline: Indian papers wary of new Pakistan administration.

text.p: Indian newspapers said on Wednesday it could take time to stabilise democracy in Pakistan after the sacking of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, and urged India not to assume that bilateral relations would improve.

"It is going to take both time and effort to stabilise democracy in Pakistan and U.S. influence on Pakistani politics is one of the determinant factors in the process, but has not always been wisely exercised," the Times of India said in an editorial.
The Hindustan Times called for more vigilence in the Himalayan region of Kashmir.
Neighbouring India and Pakistan were carved out of British India in 1947 in a blood-stained partition of the sub-continent. They have fought three wars, two of them over Kashmir.

"The (Pakistani) army-bureaucracy axis may...feel less inhibited by American coolness in significantly increasing military assistance to the Taleban in Kabul," the Hindustan Times said. "As for India, there should be stricter vigil in Kashmir."
The newspaper added it was possible the new administration might veer towards opening a dialogue with India.
"While there is no reason why India should not respond, it would be well advised not to automatically assume that a change of guard in Pakistan must necessarily improve bilateral relations," it said.

Indian officials reacted calmly on Tuesday to President Farooq Leghari's dismissal of Bhutto and her government. Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said it was an internal affair and that India had always been keen to maintain good relations.
